items.title: Apple has appointed Corey Fugman, a 26-year company veteran and former senior director of Apple Pay and Wallet, to lead its payments and dig
items.content_excerpt: Apple has appointed Corey Fugman, a 26-year company veteran and former senior director of Apple Pay and Wallet, to lead its payments and digital wallet division, according to Bloomberg. He succeeds Jennifer Bailey, who is retiring after leading the launch of Apple Pay and Wallet in 2014 but will remain as an adviser for the coming months. Fugman will oversee a multibillion-dollar contactless payments business that processes tens of billions of transactions annually across more than 90 markets, generating revenue for Apple through transaction fees. He will also supervise Apple Card, which is transitioning from Goldman Sachs to JPMorgan Chase. Fugman has been closely involved in the ongoing transfer. He will report to Services chief Eddy Cue, who oversees Apple TV, Music, Maps and iCloud. The appointment is part of a broader executive reshuffle under new CEO John Ternus, with recent changes across finance, acquisitions, legal affairs. $AAPL $GS $JPM

items.title: Microsoft disclosed that it identified a large-scale phishing campaign on November 13 targeting organizations through fraudulent Microsoft 3
items.content_excerpt: Microsoft disclosed that it identified a large-scale phishing campaign on November 13 targeting organizations through fraudulent Microsoft 365 service-health notifications. The emails falsely claimed that recipients' messages had been held due to a service disruption and warned that they would be permanently deleted within 24 hours unless users took action. The messages were designed to create urgency and trick recipients into clicking malicious links and revealing their login credentials. Microsoft said the campaign appeared primarily focused on stealing user authentication information. However, the company stressed that available evidence does not yet confirm whether credentials were successfully captured, malware was deployed, or attackers carried out additional malicious activities. The phishing operation occurred during and after last week's major Microsoft 365 outage, which affected users worldwide and disrupted Outlook. $MSFT

items.title: Microsoft's Nov 12-13 outage took down Outlook, Teams and Copilot for nearly 24 hours, and the root cause is a good lesson for every eng
items.content_excerpt: Microsoft's Nov 12-13 outage took down Outlook, Teams and Copilot for nearly 24 hours, and the root cause is a good lesson for every engineering team. It wasn't an attack. A bug that had gone unnoticed since July only showed up when extra traffic hit a gateway already down about 14% of its capacity. Failover then pushed load onto healthy servers, and over 80% ended up unresponsive. The key gap was testing: the labs didn't match real-world traffic or newer hardware. I've broken down the problem, root cause and the testing methods that could prevent it below. 👇 #Microsoft365 #Outlook #CloudOutage #SiteReliability #DevOps #SoftwareTesting #IncidentManagement #ChaosEngineering $MSFT https://victor435591.substack.com/p/the-outlook-outage-happenings-and?r=5h0e9p&utm_medium=ios

items.content_excerpt: Stanley Druckenmiller’s Duquesne Family Office significantly reshuffled its technology portfolio during the third quarter, exiting its positions in Advanced Micro Devices and Sandisk while increasing exposure to SpaceX and Palantir, according to its latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The decision to sell AMD and Sandisk shares comes amid a difficult period for semiconductor stocks, which have faced increased volatility as investors reassess AI-related valuations, growth expectations and the sustainability of massive data-center investments. However, the filing does not disclose the exact dates, transaction prices or specific reasons behind the sales. Druckenmiller’s reported purchases of SpaceX and Palantir suggest a shift in exposure toward companies positioned to benefit from artificial intelligence, software and next-generation technology infrastructure. $AMD $SNDK $SPCX $PLTR

items.content_excerpt: $SPY $QQQ A bull flag breakout sends price to 765 where you find the inside bar resistance. Also the 50 day MA as well at 764. You also find 760 resistance, the 20 and 100 day MA resistance level at 760. On Thursday if price can break all 5 resistance levels you then see another breakout to 779 to 780 resistance and price testing ATHs at 781. A double top. Then we see if price falls or consolidates. It's unlikely we see another breakout to 800 to 810 this quick. Although 3 breakouts in 1 week is always possible. But the probability is low.

items.content_excerpt: $SPY $QQQ The daily chart of $SPY looks interesting. There's a pattern forming. An uptrend from 733 to 760 which is a bull flag pole. items.content_excerpt: Bloomberg reports the Trump administration's Commerce Department issued an interim rule requiring licenses for advanced AI chips shipped to data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil to block Chinese firms' remote access. The action addresses a loophole in US export controls exposed by an alleged espionage scandal at Nvidia, where ex-CEO Jensen Huang resigned after links to a suspected Chinese intelligence operative tied to Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed. Southeast Asia's data center expansion, fueled by Chinese tech giants renting compute power, faces new hurdles, as at least 30% of China's advanced AI capacity was projected to rely on overseas rentals and smuggling by 2027. $SPY $NVDA $SMCI $BTC.X $QQQ

items.title: Omeros reported mixed Q3 2026 results, with adjusted EPS of $0.06 versus the $0.01 analyst consensus and gross YARTEMLEA revenue of $41.8 mi
items.content_excerpt: Omeros reported mixed Q3 2026 results, with adjusted EPS of $0.06 versus the $0.01 analyst consensus and gross YARTEMLEA revenue of $41.8 million, beating estimates of $37.27 million. Operating income also improved to $4.5 million from just $0.1 million in Q2. However, the Seattle-based biotech swung from a $13.2 million net profit in Q2 to a GAAP net loss of $57.4 million, or $0.79 per share, primarily due to a non-cash $62 million mark-to-market loss on a derivative linked to its convertible notes. Investor sentiment was further pressured by the European Medicines Agency's negative opinion on narsoplimab for TA-TMA following an October reexamination. Despite continued commercial progress with YARTEMLEA, the combination of the headline loss, concerns over gross-to-net revenue adjustments and regulatory setbacks weighed on shares. The broader market was relatively stable, suggesting the selloff was largely company-specific. $OMER

items.content_excerpt: $CAPR The severity of DMD combined with unmet need for something as significant as PUL is why Deramiocel will be given maximum flexibility and granted some form of approval by the FDA. Elevidys, while not my favored comparison, nonetheless is a historical precedent that shows the FDA already recognizes the extreme severity and therefore flexibility that must be applied to DMD treatments. The FDA will do everything they can to compromise and work to get this approved, because options are so few, the disease is horrific and the possibility of preserving hand and arm function is so vitally important to a human's quality of life. The data has been disputed, but rare disease approvals are not solely decided on data driven arguments. The FDA is a rigorous organization, but it is able to be flexible in this arena. The FDA will err on the side of making treatments available to patients in severe, rare diseases targeting an unmet need. We will see that here! CAPR has a strong pathway to approval!

items.title: President Donald Trump told reporters that he has no plans to replace Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, despite recent scrutiny over Lutnic
items.content_excerpt: President Donald Trump told reporters that he has no plans to replace Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, despite recent scrutiny over Lutnick’s handling of export controls for Nvidia’s advanced AI chips Lutnick has repeatedly delayed (rumour - 3 times) efforts to crack down on companies suspected of diverting these chips to China. This disagreement reportedly sparked a confrontation in the Situation Room b/n Lutnick & Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Bessent noted that the Depts of Treasury, Defense, & State, along w/ the USTR, had all supported adding the company Megaspeed to the trade "entity list" for months While President Trump acknowledged that Lutnick may have held up Megaspeed’s addition to the list, he defended the move as necessary to preserve diplomatic ties. "He was doing that because you could have — if you didn’t delay it, if you didn’t do something — you could have a blow-up with China," President Trump explained. "We’re having a very good relationship w/ China right now, & I understand both sides of it, & I’ll make a decision. But I understand very well both sides." Meanwhile, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to the President in early spring warning him about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged relationship w/ a suspected Chinese spy. Rumours: Rubio may have taken liberties to the CIA report & recast Alice Huang as a China spy - currently, evidence supports that she was merely a smuggler & an opportunist - the CIA officials were"not yet convinced" that Alice Huang knowingly passed intelligence to Beijing When asked about the memo, however, President Trump stated, "I haven’t heard that." Rumour: The memo was leaked by Rubio’s office - Rubio has a reputation as a prominent China hawk. Rubio & other national security hawks inside the admin were reportedly frustrated by Jensen Huang's direct access to President Trump & the admin's willingness to allow certain AI chip sales to China Note: The memo was originally drafted and circulated in the spring—ahead of Trump's May trip to Beijing & sat dormant for months. Releasing it immediately after the midterm elections maximized its political and corporate impact while avoiding market turmoil, voter backlash, or a diplomatic incident with China before ballots were cast $NVDA $SOXS $KWEB $FXI $SPY

stocks.name: SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc
stocks.summary: SELLAS is drawing attention ahead of the anticipated Phase 3 REGAL readout for galinpepimut-S (GPS) in AML, following the trials 80th event milestone. Traders are interpreting volatile after-hours moves as possible positioning or a data leak, though neither is confirmed; bullish hopes for strong results and a potential buyout compete with skepticism about the trials outcome and bearish signals.
